source.title: Fourier fractal dimension to predict the generalization of deep neural networks

record.tranche_reason: The study measures a different property—the Fourier dimension of weight variations—and reports its correlation with the generalization gap. It does not test the version about magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.gate_note: The paper reports Kendall correlations between its proposed Fourier measure and the generalization gap on three datasets. Figure 4 compares optimizer training dynamics, but the text gives no specific test-error result for that comparison.
record.test_reason: Table 1 evaluates PAC-Bayes magnitude flatness, a magnitude-aware sharpness measure defined in Jiang et al., against generalization gaps and norm/margin measures in new experiments. This bears on V7, although the proposed Fourier measure itself fits no version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: Fourier dimension predicts generalization gaps, and their optimizer is presented as improving stability and generalization. Their assertion of the highest correlation on every dataset is contradicted by Table 1: on SVHN, PAC-Bayes origin scores 0.676 versus Fourier's 0.672. Figure 4 does not establish a specific held-out-performance improvement.
record.recipe_differences: Measures Fourier dimension of weight variations and proposes a Fourier-based optimizer; it does not apply the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: Figure 3 reports that deeper layer combinations tend to show stronger correlations with the gap; no numerical layer-combination values are given in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: Fourier dimension correlates with the generalization gap: Kendall τ is 0.680 on CIFAR-10, 0.672 on SVHN, and 0.551 on MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fourier dimension of weight variations predicts generalization-gap rankings in the evaluated convolutional models.

record.problems: The text does not state the number of models or runs summarized for the correlations, and reports no uncertainty estimates. The layer-combination results are described without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 also reports correlations for numerous comparison measures. Those comparison rows were omitted to keep the extraction focused on the study's proposed measure; the comparisons are summarized in the authors_conclusion. Figure 4's optimizer curves were not extracted because the text does not state a specific test-error result.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and corresponding natural-label and random-label held-out performance.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Whether models reach similarly low training loss, whether augmentation is absent, and the precise architecture and hyperparameter population are not established. No causal relationship is tested.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Add V7-linked rows for PAC-Bayes magnitude flatness (0.149, 0.584, 0.364) and inverse-margin comparisons (0.473, 0.657, 0.386), respectively on CIFAR-10, SVHN, and MNIST. Although comparison measures are declared omitted, these rows are needed to represent the version actually tested.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. V7 relevance rests on the PAC-Bayes magnitude-flatness comparison, not Fourier dimension or discussion of wide minima. Model counts, uncertainty, and detailed experimental controls are unspecified.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
Network width and test error around or beyond the interpolation threshold are not tested.
Convolutional and fully connected architectures are not compared.
Adaptive optimizers are not compared with SGD for held-out performance.
Batch size and its effect on held-out performance are not tested.
Dropout and weight decay effects are not tested.
The study measures Fourier dimension, not magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures under the specified conditions.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy are not tested.

relationships.reason: Text/table-based verdict pending comparison rows: magnitude flatness correlates positively with the gap (0.149, 0.584, 0.364), but inverse margin ranks it better on every dataset (0.473, 0.657, 0.386). Thus the association appears, while its comparative ranking needs qualification.
relationships.display_finding: The available evidence does not confirm the reported positive associations between flatness and generalization gaps or the stronger rankings from inverse margin across the three datasets.
